datasets.evidence: We extracted peptide sequences from the PeptideAtlas [24] database (accessed December 2024). This resulted in 1,725,301 unique peptides, of which 1,656,289 were used for training and 69,012 for validation.

datasets.positive_samples: 7,343 training, 918 validation, 919 test (AMP sequences with MIC values)
datasets.evidence: We used the DBAASP v3 [25] database, which contains AMP sequences and MIC values for various bacterial strains. After manual curation, the dataset was divided into 7343 training, 918 validation, and 919 test samples, all derived from 35 bacterial strains.
Fulltext: 'a collection of peptides with lengths less than or equal to 32 was gathered from UniProt, resulting in a dataset comprising 630,683 peptides.'
Fulltext: 'a curated set of 9896 positive samples and 2403 negative samples were retrieved from various AMP databases.'

metrics.metric_name: Activity probability (by CAMP, AMP Scanner, Macrel)
metrics.usage: Used to evaluate generated AMP sequences; percentage of peptides identified as AMPs by all three predictors.
metrics.evidence: Fulltext: 'we used three different AMP classifiers: The predictor based on the collection of anti-microbial peptides (CAMP), AMP Scanner, and Macrel, to assess their potential for bioactivity... the percentage of the peptide sequences identified as AMPs by all three predictors simultaneously (with predicted values of 0.5 or higher).'

important_evidence: AMP-RL: GPT-2 based transformer with RL and LoRA for strain-specific optimization; code available at https://github.com/GIST-CSBL/AMP-RL.
AMP-MIC: Based on AMP-GPT; predicts MIC for specific bacterial species; code available at https://github.com/jkwang93/AMP-Designer.
AMP-Designer described in review as GPT-based framework with knowledge distillation and RL.
PeptideAtlas and DBAASP v3 used as datasets for AMP-RL.
UniProt peptides (630,683) and AMP databases (9896 positive, 2403 negative) used for AMP-GPT/AMP-MIC.
uncertainties: Full-text verification needed for HydrAMP, PepCVAE, PrefixProt, MoFormer, HMAMP, and AMP-Designer to confirm code availability and exact model details.
No direct links to PeptideAtlas or DBAASP v3 provided; these need to be sourced from the original publications.
The review mentions AMP-RL as a new model; its benchmark suitability depends on independent evaluation and availability of trained weights.

The fulltext for PMID 29679519 appears to be from a different paper (likely about AMP-Designer). The actual paper 'Designing Anticancer Peptides by Constructive Machine Learning' may not contain AMP-Designer. Need to verify correct source of AMP-MIC and AMP-Designer.
Review paper (PMID:35128926) might mention AMP prediction models, but fulltext not available to extract details.
